summary: JIT provisioning failure for 'Redwood Analytics' SAML app leads to missing analytics roles for new hires
description:
Issue summary: New employees and contractors created after a recent change to the Analytics SAML app fail to receive the expected 'analytics:viewer' or 'analytics:editor' roles via Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning. Impact: Affected users can authenticate via Okta SSO but land in the analytics console with no roles and 'access denied' when attempting to load dashboards. This blocks onboarding and on-call access for a subset of infra/ops engineers. Environment: prod (us-east).

Observed behavior: Users successfully SSO into the Analytics UI, but the internal identity service logs show JIT provisioning rejected due to SAML assertion audience mismatch or missing role attribute. Expected behavior: Okta SAML response should be accepted and JIT should create the user with roles derived from the SAML attribute mapping.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a test Okta user in the same group used for new hires (okta-group: infra-analytics).
2) Trigger SSO to https://analytics.internal.redwood.ai using Okta (SAML redirect).
3) Inspect identity service logs for the SAML Assertion handling and JIT flow.

Observed logs: see 'logs' field. Temporary workaround: Manual user creation with roles via identity admin CLI and short-term rollback of the proxy entityID change applied to the analytics SAML app. Workaround applied 2026-03-13 18:40 UTC restored access for ~70% of affected users; remaining accounts require manual role grant.

Investigation summary: The analytics SAML app's entityID was changed on 2026-03-12 as part of an internal routing change (added ':proxy' suffix to support multi-tenant routing through a reverse proxy). The JIT handler validates the SAML Audience/Recipient strictly against a single accepted entityID ('urn:redwood:analytics') and therefore rejects assertions with 'urn:redwood:analytics:proxy'. Additionally, when the SAML assertion is accepted by a fallback path, the role attribute mapping is occasionally absent for SCIM-provisioned contractor accounts, causing a no-role state. The combination of a stricter audience check and inconsistent role attribute mapping explains the partial rollback success.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term: Expand JIT acceptedAudience list to include 'urn:redwood:analytics:proxy' and run a reconciler to grant roles to accounts created without attributes. (Owner: identity infra)
- Medium term: Update Okta app metadata to standardize entityID (preferred) and remove proxy-suffixed entityIDs; update routing so proxies preserve original entityID in the SAML flow. (Owner: infra)
- Add an automated smoke test for JIT provisioning during deploys and a post-change reconcile job to find accounts with no roles.

Impact metrics: ~18 affected accounts identified so far (mix of full-time and contractors). Severity classified Sev2 due to operational but not company-wide outage.
